title: K-flat criteria
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $T$ a scheme. Work on a small skeleton of $T_{\Et}$ in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-etale-site; def-weil-size-convention], with the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Complexes and K-flatness use the direct-sum total tensor convention of [def-kun-derived-tensor]; flat sheaves mean tensor-flat sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

(1) Every bounded-above complex of flat $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves is K-flat.

(2) In a distinguished triangle in the homotopy category $K(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_T))$ (complexes modulo chain homotopy, with distinguished triangles the triangles isomorphic to mapping-cone triangles [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]), if two terms are K-flat, so is the third. In particular, the cone of a morphism between K-flat complexes is K-flat.

(3) For every small filtered category $I$ and diagram $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ of K-flat complexes, the degreewise sheaf colimit $\varinjlim_i K_i^\bullet$ is K-flat. In particular, a complex expressed as a small filtered degreewise colimit of bounded-above complexes of flat sheaves is K-flat.

proof.text: For (1), take the ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)=(T_{\Et},\Lambda_T)$. The flatness and K-flatness conventions are precisely those in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] to this site and the given bounded-above complex. Its hypotheses require only an upper degree bound and tensor-flat terms, both assumed; it supplies acyclicity after tensor with every acyclic complex, with no lower degree bound.

For a mapping-cone triangle $K_1\to K_2\to C(f)\to K_1[1]$, fix any acyclic complex $A$. By [def-kun-derived-tensor], the two K-flat terms give acyclic total tensor complexes with $A$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-cone-two-out-of-three], with the acyclic factor on the left, to obtain acyclicity for the third tensor complex. The sign symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in bidegree $(p,q)$ identifies this with the convention of [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Since $A$ was arbitrary, the third term is K-flat. This proves the cone assertion.

For a general distinguished triangle in the homotopy category, [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated] identifies it up to homotopy-category isomorphism with a mapping-cone triangle. K-flatness is invariant under these isomorphisms: if $h:K^q\to L^{q-1}$ is a chain homotopy, on $A^p\otimes K^q$ use $H=(-1)^p(1\otimes h)$. For the total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the two terms involving $d_A$ cancel and $dH+Hd=1\otimes(dh+hd)$. Thus tensor carries homotopy inverse maps to homotopy inverse maps. Such maps induce inverse maps on cohomology, since $dh+hd$ acts trivially on cycles modulo boundaries. Hence tensor acyclicity, and so K-flatness [def-kun-derived-tensor], transfers along the three isomorphisms; the preceding step proves (2).

proof.text: For (3), fix any acyclic complex $A$. The small-skeleton convention [def-weil-size-convention] satisfies the small-site hypothesis of [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. That node identifies $\operatorname{Tot}((\varinjlim_i K_i)\otimes A)$ with $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Tot}(K_i\otimes A)$ and says filtered module-sheaf colimits are exact. Every tensor complex on the right is acyclic by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. More explicitly, set $C_i=\operatorname{Tot}(K_i\otimes A)$ and $Z_i^n=\ker d_{C_i}^n$. Acyclicity gives short exact sequences $0\to Z_i^n\to C_i^n\to Z_i^{n+1}\to0$, compatible with transition maps. Exactness of the filtered colimit gives the same sequences with colimits, and $\colim Z_i^{n+1}\to\colim C_i^{n+1}$ is monic. Therefore the image of the colimit differential in degree $n-1$ and the kernel of its differential in degree $n$ are both $\colim Z_i^n$. The colimit complex is acyclic. As $A$ was arbitrary, the colimit is K-flat. The final assertion follows by applying (1) to each diagram term and then this result.
